text: How strongly a lens bends light toward or away from its axis, measured as one divided by the focal length expressed in metres.

When a beam of light passes through a colloidal solution, its path turns visible because the colloidal particles throw the light sideways; shorter wavelengths are scattered preferentially, which is why the sky looks blue and sunsets red.
For a metallic conductor kept at one temperature, the current flowing through it grows in step with the voltage applied between its ends.
A rule that tells which way the field wraps when current flows through a straight wire.
Higher groupings share fewer features: climbing from species up to kingdom, the traits any two members still have in common keep dropping.
Plants are grouped using their vegetative and reproductive traits; animals are grouped on overall body resemblance.
Often called the plant kingdom's amphibians, since water is essential for their sexual reproduction.
Vertebrates with two pairs of limbs, living on land or in water; the group spans amphibians (Amphibia), reptiles (Reptilia), birds (Aves), and mammals (Mammalia).
How flowers sit along the floral axis: in the racemose type the axis keeps growing, while in the cymose type it ends in a flower.
A flower carries four whorls - calyx, corolla, androecium, gynoecium - and is grouped by symmetry into actinomorphic, zygomorphic, or asymmetric types.
The two-step cell division that halves the chromosome number, yielding haploid gametes.
Splitting of water replaces the electrons PS II loses and gives off oxygen in the process.
Air left in the lungs even after breathing out normally.
How much air can be pushed out at most after the deepest possible intake, or breathed in after the deepest exhale.
How much blood each ventricle pumps out in one minute, obtained as heart rate times the stroke volume.
The skeleton's central part - skull, vertebral column, sternum and ribs - 80 bones in all.
Nerve cables of the peripheral nervous system that carry sensory signals inward to the central axis, or motor commands outward to muscles and glands.
When elements stand in rising atomic-weight order, look-alike properties come back at regular intervals.
A bigger effective nuclear charge makes ionization enthalpy larger; a bigger atomic radius makes it smaller.
The many spatial forms ethane takes as its two methyl groups spin about the C-C single bond; staggered sits lowest in energy, eclipsed highest.
A body keeps doing what it is doing - staying at rest or moving uniformly in a straight line - until a net external force makes it change.
The friction that must be overcome before one surface starts sliding over another.
Pressure applied anywhere on an enclosed fluid travels to every part of the fluid without loss.
When two identical waves moving contrary ways meet on a string with both ends fixed, the result is a stationary pattern of nodes and antinodes.
The transfer of pollen from anther to stigma - same flower (autogamy), another flower of the same plant (geitonogamy), or a different plant (xenogamy).
Two fusions happen together in the embryo sac: syngamy forms the diploid zygote, while triple fusion yields the triploid primary endosperm nucleus.
Complete well-being - physical, mental, emotional and social - in all matters of the reproductive system, backed at the national level by programmes such as RCH.
Pills, injections or implants carrying progestogen alone or with estrogen; they stop ovulation and block implantation.
Deliberately ending a pregnancy before it reaches full term, under legal safeguards that guard against misuse.
Fertilisation done outside the body (in vitro), after which the early embryo is placed into the woman's reproductive tract.
ZIFT places embryos of up to eight blastomeres into the fallopian tube; IUT puts embryos beyond that stage into the uterus.
A back-of-the-envelope count of yearly conceptions worldwide: MTPs are known to make up about one fifth of all conceptions, so multiplying MTP numbers by five estimates the total.
Molecular scissors that read a specific palindromic stretch of double-stranded DNA and slice each backbone at a set point within it.
Large reaction vessels (100-1000 litres) where raw material is turned into a specific product by cells of microbes, plants, animals or humans, kept under conditions that suit their growth best.
How many ligand donor atoms are bonded straight to the central metal ion.
Haloalkanes and haloarenes are sorted by how many halogen atoms they carry and by the kind of carbon (sp3 or sp2) that holds the halogen.
Organometallics with a carbon-metal bond; the classic case is the alkylmagnesium halide (Grignard reagent), made by adding magnesium to a haloalkane in dry ether.
Grignards are so reactive toward any proton donor that every trace of moisture must be kept away; water would turn them into hydrocarbons.
Alcohols carry -OH groups on sp3 carbon while phenols have -OH straight on the ring; both families are sorted by how many -OH groups are present and how substituted that carbon is.
Alcohols boil well above hydrocarbons of about the same molar mass because their molecules hydrogen-bond to each other.
The Lucas test mixes concentrated HCl with anhydrous ZnCl2: a cloudy layer appears at different speeds for primary, secondary or tertiary alcohols, which is how they are told apart.

Oxidation or catalytic dehydrogenation turns 1-degree alcohols into aldehydes and 2-degree ones into ketones; alkenes cleave in ozonolysis, and alkynes add water under catalysis, again giving carbonyl compounds.
Three routes to ketones: acyl chlorides plus dialkylcadmium, nitriles treated with a Grignard reagent and then hydrolysed, or Friedel-Crafts acylation of arenes.

The carboxyl group (-COOH, suffixed -oic acid) holds a planar carbon whose electrophilicity is reduced relative to an ordinary carbonyl carbon, because resonance from the hydroxyl oxygen donates electron density onto it.
Made by oxidising primary alcohols, aldehydes or alkylbenzenes; by hydrolysing nitriles, amides, acid chlorides or even esters; or from Grignard reagents plus dry ice.
The C-O-C bridge joining two monosaccharide rings; water is eliminated as the oxygen bridge forms.
The work an external agency must do to assemble a set of charges from infinitely far apart, placing each at its position; that stored work is the configuration's electrostatic potential energy.
A single worldwide measurement standard: the International System of Units (SI), whose base unit of length is the metre.
Materials split by whether electric current can travel through them: current-passing ones are conductors, current-blocking ones are insulators.
A magnet hung freely so it can swing settles pointing along the geographic north-south line.
Millions of microscopic finger-shaped folds lining the small intestine from inside; they widen the absorbing surface so nutrients pass into the blood more easily.
Insects breathe through a tube network: air enters through side pores (spiracles) and travels along branching tracheae to the tissues.
In the cell symbol, the longer thin line stands for the positive terminal; the shorter thick one stands for the negative terminal.
A battery is a chain of two or more cells wired so each cell's positive side feeds the next cell's negative side.
Dirty household water carrying dissolved and suspended matter - organic waste, salts, plant nutrients and disease-causing microbes.
Male and female gametes meet and fuse; the zygote so formed grows into a new individual.
Friction always pushes against the way surfaces slide, slowing moving things down.
A push or pull from a distance: one charged body acting on another body, charged or not.
A glass funnel with a tap, used to part two liquids that do not mix and settle in layers, drawing on their density difference.
A light beam becomes visible inside a colloid or suspension because its particles scatter the light sideways.
How many nucleons - protons plus neutrons - sit in an atom's nucleus; written as A.
For a covalent molecule, add up the atomic masses of every atom in one molecule; the total comes in unified atomic mass units (u).
For an ionic compound, the atomic masses are totaled over its simplest formula unit instead of a molecule.
Sound Navigation And Ranging: ultrasonic pulses sent into water reveal how far away, in which direction and how fast underwater objects move.
All life sorted into five kingdoms - Monera, Protista, Fungi, then Plantae and Animalia - mainly on cell structure, body organisation and how each obtains food.
Earth works as one connected whole whose five spheres - the solid geosphere, watery hydrosphere, icy cryosphere, gaseous atmosphere and living biosphere - constantly interact.
